features.description: Specify the first desktop workspace, terminal, draft recovery and NOLF integration slice.
acceptance_criteria: Carry forward macOS/Windows, empty-to-split layout, movable tabs, basic editing/optional Vim, persistent sidecar sessions, the session browser and multiple project/worktree roots with explicit per-session bindings as confirmed requirements.

Pin the owner-selected flat NOLF host build/profile; specify actual rendered output/input in a new tab, native host ownership and acceptance commands on both platforms, with VtMB as the second adapter.

Specify stable root identities and local recovery drafts with explicit file saves; define checkpoint/conflict handling, initial Vim subset and predeclared measurable terminal/editor/game budgets; keep agent installers, Quest and XR as later gates.
features.deliverable: docs/specs/032-desktop-v0.md

features.description: Qualify the desktop UI, terminal and game-surface stack on macOS and Windows.
acceptance_criteria: Compare a small set of existing layout/editor/terminal components against native desktop and later Quest-client constraints with source/license/version references.
On both platforms demonstrate a real PTY, editable text/Vim-mode feasibility and a real cooperative graphical surface with resize/input; static mockups are insufficient.
Measure agreed budgets and choose an implementation stack with known limits and rollback; failure produces a revised proposal, not a supported-platform claim.
features.deliverable: docs/decisions/desktop-stack.md and bounded feasibility prototype

features.description: Implement the empty workspace with recursive splits and movable tab groups.
acceptance_criteria: Start empty, split horizontally/vertically, resize and collapse splits, and open/reorder/move tabs between pane groups.
Keyboard/pointer focus follows the intended tab; moving a view preserves its session and root binding and does not trigger a new session or change another tab's context.
Exercise the actual UI on macOS and Windows, including minimum sizes and displays with different scaling.
features.deliverable: orchestrator layout implementation and UI evidence

features.description: Implement a desktop sidecar that owns interactive sessions independently of views.
acceptance_criteria: Session records identify owning sidecar, stable project/worktree root, type, target, launch cwd, process/PTY identity and state; launch only through explicit commands and distinguish shell cwd from launch association.
Closing a view or GUI leaves sessions alive; reconnect attaches to the same session; explicit Stop terminates the intended process tree and reports exit.

Test sessions in two separate worktrees, GUI loss, sidecar failure, missing roots and stale identities on macOS/Windows; never retarget a session by focus/display name or claim a terminated process has resumed.
features.deliverable: sidecar session service and lifecycle tests

features.description: Connect real terminal panes to sidecar-owned PTY sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise an interactive shell/full-screen terminal program with input, resize, scrollback, Unicode, paste and control keys on both desktops.

Move/detach/reattach terminals bound to different roots without losing their process and retained output; focus routes input only to the selected session and a shell cwd change does not rebind its launch root.
Long-lived sessions have no inherited verification-job deadline; measure responsiveness and retain failure/exit state.
features.deliverable: terminal provider and desktop acceptance evidence

features.description: Provide project tree, previews and basic text editing with optional Vim mode.
acceptance_criteria: Browse multiple declared roots, preview files, and edit/save text with undo/redo/search, dirty-buffer status and external-change handling; identical relative filenames in separate worktrees retain distinct root-bound buffers and save destinations.
Exercise the F32-defined Vim subset and ordinary editing on macOS/Windows; preserve supported encoding/line endings and avoid silent overwrite of external edits.

Retain unsaved edits as local recovery drafts on view close/GUI restart and write working files only on explicit Save; exercise external edits, checkpoint failure and explicit Discard without losing the only unsaved copy; large/binary/unsupported files fail or preview explicitly.
features.deliverable: file/tree/editor providers and edit-path evidence

features.description: Persist layout and recover views onto retained sessions after GUI restart.
acceptance_criteria: Restore splits, tab placement, stable root/session associations and durable local editor drafts after closing/reopening the GUI with multiple projects/worktrees; no restore path silently writes working files.
Resolve live session IDs through the sidecar; no restore path relaunches commands automatically or confuses a dead process with a live one.

Interrupted saves and unknown persistence versions recover with an actionable result; test macOS/Windows paths and changed/missing/removed roots without silently remapping sessions, relaunching commands or stopping retained processes.
features.deliverable: versioned workspace persistence and recovery evidence

features.description: Implement the terminal-based Bash agent selector and extensible launch registry.
acceptance_criteria: Discover supported installed CLI agents and allow an explicit custom installed command; launch in the chosen terminal's explicit root and launch directory regardless of another tab's focused project.
Keep recipes/version detection outside pane code and specify the Windows Bash/native-or-WSL path contract without guessing conversions.
Prove selection/launch both inside the orchestrator and standalone on macOS/Windows, including missing agent and cancelled selection.

features.description: Add visible selected-agent installation and recoverable setup recipes.

features.description: Record a live game pane: a rolling buffer by default, a toggle on the game tab that commits a segment from the ring or from an explicit start/stop, and committed segments queryable over MCP as timestamped keyframes, a log slice and a manifest on one clock.
acceptance_criteria: The ring holds JPEG keyframes encoded as they arrive, never raw frames, through third_party/stb/stb_image_write.h pinned at the stb revision third_party/sources.json already records; orchestrator/native/recording.c bounds it by seconds AND bytes with defaults 120 s / 64 MiB / 10 fps / 640 px / quality 70, read from the validated workspace preference recording and clamped again in the desktop, and the game tab's row shows the bound it actually applied. rengine_recording_test (CTest native_recording) covers both bounds, the declared sample rate, the bottom-up-to-top-down flip, commit-last-N, explicit start/stop, an explicit segment that outruns the ring reporting truncated with droppedLeadMs, a commit draining over ticks with its manifest written last, a session exit committing an open segment, and a close finishing a drain.

A segment is <root>/.cache/recordings/<id>/ with a self-ignoring .gitignore, manifest.json (version 1, written last so an incomplete commit is not listed), keyframes.jsonl, keyframes/NNNNNN.jpg and log.jsonl; every keyframe and every log line carries atMs, an absolute wall time and, for keyframes, the game frame sequence, so an agent can put a frame beside the line printed while it was on screen. Audio is a declared slot naming capture-mcp and KI-044 rather than a silent omission; no second audio stack and no video container are built here.

orchestrator/server/recordings.mjs serves listRecordings/readRecording as a pure filesystem read; the session host and the replaceable workspace worker both answer GET /api/recordings and GET /api/recording from it and both advertise recordings: 1, so a layered workspace update alone delivers the capability (spec 078's asymmetry, KI-043) and supervisor.mjs claims nothing; recordings_list and recording_read are read-only MCP tools gated by that flag with the workspace-layer remedy. A native fixture (native-recording.spec.mjs, in test:desktop) drives the toggle against a real frame stream, commits both gestures and reads the committed segment back. npm test, npm run test:desktop, CTest, ./init.sh, design.py check, features.py validate and sidecar validation pass with zero native warnings. Passing waits on the owner's live verification after a layered update, as F71/F72/F74 do.

features.description: Contract 4 devices: a project declares where each target runs, rEngine probes reachability under the declared-command boundary and reports availability in those terms, replacing the tools-on-PATH proxy and the local executable stat for non-local targets.
acceptance_criteria: contract accepts 1, 2, 3 and 4; contract 4 adds the optional top-level devices array (1-8 records of id, kind local|ssh|adb, title, optional host/selector each exactly one of value|env, requires, tools, probe, probeTimeoutMs) and an optional device on a game record and a dashboard action defaulting to local. Declaring devices, or any device key, under contract 3 is rejected by version naming requires contract 4 and the declared contract, never by unknown key; contracts 1-3 read unchanged and both live consumer declarations (vtmb-vr, nolf-improved) still read clean.

Device rules are named cross-field errors: unique kebab ids, the reserved local id/kind pairing with at most one local device and no probe/host/selector on it, exactly one of value|env on host and selector, a probe placeholder whose source is not declared, and an unknown device reference on a game or action listing the declared ids and local.

A target bound to a non-local device is never resolved or stat-ed against the local filesystem: inspectGame reports the device, its reachability and the target's own (still local) requires, names where the executable lives, and the message Game executable not found no longer appears for it. Availability composes device reachability with the target's own requires/tools and names the failing half.

Probes run under the same execution boundary as every other declared command (no shell, cwd the project root, shell environment, stdin closed, bounded output, default 5000 ms capped at 60000, killed as a process group on timeout) and only on an explicit availability check or refresh, never on a timer or during tree listing. Exit 0 is reachable; non-zero or timeout is unreachable with the first stderr line as the reason; a missing or empty host/selector env is unreachable by name without a spawn; device requires/tools short-circuit before the probe.
Probe results are cached per root, device and resolved argv for 15 s with in-flight coalescing so one dashboard listing probes each device once, and an explicit refresh bypasses the cache.

GET /api/devices?rootId[&refresh] is served by the replaceable workspace worker, which advertises projectDevices: 1 (spec 078 / KI-043: a capability served only by the retained host cannot be delivered by a layered update); a read-only MCP devices tool is gated on it and game_preflight/dashboard_actions report device-derived availability. launch_game on a non-local device refuses by name, naming the project's own script actions bound to that device, and attempts nothing.

A native Devices section lists declared devices with status, a manual refresh and the targets bound to each, showing one reason for an unreachable device rather than repeating it per action, through the owned control layer and generated RE_METRIC_*/RE_COLOR_* constants. npm test, npm run test:desktop, CTest, ./init.sh, python3 tools/design.py check, features.py validate and the sidecar check pass, and a native fixture covers the Devices section including the unreachable case.

features.description: A third game surface, cooperative: rEngine reserves the surface and passes RENGINE_SURFACE_PORT/RENGINE_SURFACE_TOKEN exactly as embedded does but injects nothing, so a game whose own engine speaks the surface protocol -- a statically linked or non-SDL2 runtime the adapter can never interpose -- gets a live workspace pane instead of falling back to its own window.
acceptance_criteria: The surface enum is embedded | external | cooperative and needs no contract bump: it is a new value of a closed enum, so a reader that predates it refuses the document and drops the whole games array rather than degrading, and nothing on the injection path tests anything but equality with embedded. Both directions are tested: the current schema refuses an unknown value naming all three, and a reconstruction of the predecessor enum refuses cooperative and yields no games.

A cooperative launch composes the record's own env plus RENGINE_SURFACE_PORT and RENGINE_SURFACE_TOKEN and NO DYLD_/LD_ key at all, asserted on the environment rEngine composes rather than on the child's, because macOS purges DYLD_* before a protected interpreter can report it. This is the regression that keeps the two-producer race unreachable by configuration: an injected adapter and a self-connecting game would greet the same token on one channel, surfaces.mjs destroys whichever socket arrives second, and both sides reconnect.

Preflight reports no adapter and no platform issue for a cooperative record on any platform: the macOS adapter precondition and the needs host integration and qualification on this platform issue stay with embedded, because a cooperative game is portable by construction. embedded on macOS still composes DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES with the adapter and external still reserves nothing.
The contract-4 rule binding a streaming game to the local device covers cooperative through the same code and the same message as embedded, named once in game-rules.mjs rather than tested twice.

The session stays type game carrying its surface, so the native pane, the /surface upgrade, Sessions and Stop behave as they do for embedded, verified rather than assumed: a native fixture launches a cooperative game through the real game route and shows a rising frame sequence, surface cooperative in the snapshot and none of the external tab's PTY text or status row. Launch identity, coalescing and the different-arguments refusal are unchanged.

The suite never depends on a consumer binary: a committed fixture producer reads the two variables, greets both channels through the server's own encoder, streams frames and reports the injection variables it was handed. npm test, npm run test:desktop, CTest, ./init.sh, python3 tools/design.py check, features.py validate and the sidecar check pass, the native build has zero warnings, and the real-NOLF qualification still passes unchanged since NOLF stays embedded.
